legalNotice.title: Plenya operates under Brazilian law.
legalNotice.body: The full text of this policy is available only in Portuguese, as it governs services regulated by Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018) and the Brazilian Federal Council of Medicine (CFM). The Portuguese version below is the authoritative version. If you have questions in English, please reach out to our Data Protection Officer at the email below.

checkup.metaDescription: Checkup oriented to your health trajectory: VO₂ max, ApoB, body composition, sleep, cognition. Maps the silent window before symptoms appear. Plenya, Londrina, Brazil.
checkup.ogDescription: Clinical assessment oriented to the trajectory of health — not just to diagnosing established disease.
checkup.schemaDescription: Clinical assessment oriented to the trajectory of health — VO₂ max, ApoB, body composition, sleep, cognition. Maps the silent window before symptoms appear.
checkup.heroP: A traditional checkup confirms whether you are sick today. A longevity checkup maps where your health is heading over the next twenty years — and what is still in time to change.
checkup.aboutP1: Conventional medicine validates normality. Longevity medicine reads trajectory. They are different questions — and they require different instruments.
checkup.aboutP2: In Brazil, most annual checkups are still designed to identify already-established disease. CBC, glucose, total cholesterol, abdominal ultrasound — useful, but insufficient. ApoB predicts cardiovascular risk better than LDL. VO₂ max predicts all-cause mortality better than any other single marker. Body composition by bioimpedance distinguishes those who lost fat from those who lost muscle. These are the exams that change decisions.
checkup.aboutP3: The Plenya longevity checkup is structured in three layers. The first, advanced laboratory tests — ApoB-centered lipid profile, inflammatory markers, minerals and vitamins that regulate cellular function. The second, functional assessment — cardiopulmonary exercise testing for VO₂ max, dynamometry, segmental bioimpedance. The third, habit and environment assessment — measured sleep, light exposure, eating pattern, physical activity tracked by wearable.
checkup.aboutP4: The result is not an envelope with red marks. It is a 90-minute conversation with integrated clinical reading and a named plan — substance, dose, frequency, re-evaluation deadline.
checkup.aside1_4: 25-OH vitamin D, B12, omega-3 index, magnesium
checkup.faq1A: It is a clinical assessment oriented not just to detecting established disease, but to mapping the trajectory of health — cardiorespiratory capacity, body composition, advanced metabolic markers, sleep, cognition, habits. The goal is to identify the silent window between normal and optimal, before symptoms appear.
checkup.faq2Q: How does it differ from the traditional checkup?
checkup.faq2A: The traditional checkup validates normality within wide reference ranges. The longevity checkup integrates markers that predict trajectory — VO₂ max, ApoB, Lp(a), body composition, omega-3 index — and crosses them with habits, sleep, and exposures. It is not a "normal" stamp; it is a plan.
checkup.faq3A: The base panel includes advanced lipid profile (ApoB, Lp(a)), HbA1c, fasting and post-prandial glucose, hs-CRP, vitamin D, ferritin, B12, homocysteine, omega-3 index, magnesium, thyroid hormones, vitamin K2 (when indicated), 25-OH vitamin D. Functional assessment includes cardiopulmonary exercise testing (VO₂ max), bioimpedance, grip dynamometry. Imaging is risk-driven — we do not use scanning without indication.
checkup.faq4A: The Plenya longevity checkup is a process, not a single day. Lab collection happens in one morning. The clinical-reading session, with individualized plan, lasts 90 minutes. Patients who join the Continuum program have re-evaluation every six months.
checkup.faq5Q: What age is it indicated for?
checkup.faq5A: The most valuable window is between 35 and 55 years old — before damage takes hold, after the first silent changes. Above 55, it is still useful to reverse what is reversible and stabilize the rest. Below 35, it makes sense for people with a family history of early cardiovascular events.
checkup.faq6A: The Plenya consultation is private-pay. Some labs may be covered by your insurance plan in Brazil — we advise the best strategy case by case. Most patients prefer to consolidate everything at a partner laboratory to ensure standardized technique and longitudinal comparability.
checkup.scheduleDesc: Reach out to the Plenya team to understand the best format for your moment — a Plenya Consultation or the Continuum program.

renal.metaTitle: Preventive kidney assessment — nephrology before symptoms
renal.metaDescription: The kidney is the silent organ. Preventive assessment with cystatin C, albuminuria, eGFR, and integrated nephrology reading. Dr. Getúlio Amaral Filho · Plenya · Londrina, Brazil.
renal.ogDescription: Detect the silent window in which kidney damage is still reversible.
renal.schemaDescription: Detect the silent window in which kidney damage is still reversible. Cystatin C, albuminuria, eGFR, and integrated nephrology reading.
renal.heroTitle: The kidney is the silent organ.
renal.heroP: It loses function on a curve, with no symptoms. By the time it hurts, the damage is past the window. Preventive kidney assessment looks at the kidney in the phase when there is still time to change the trajectory.
renal.whyP1: Approximately 10% of the Brazilian adult population has some degree of chronic kidney disease. More than 90% don't know it. The kidney signals only after losing more than half of its function — and by then, much of what is lost does not come back.
renal.whyP2: That is why the preventive nephrology approach changes the agenda. We don't wait for creatinine to rise; we read cystatin C, albuminuria, urinary sediment, and 24-hour blood pressure pattern. We cross with the cardiometabolic profile — because the kidney and heart share a damage pathway. We adjust medications that overload the kidney before they cause a problem. We treat hypertension for nephroprotection, not just for the number.
renal.whyP3Part1: Plenya's preventive kidney assessment is led by
renal.whyP3Part2: , a nephrologist (CRM-PR 21.876 · RQE 16.038), faculty member, and coordinator of the nephrology medical residency at Santa Casa de Londrina. The reading is specific: every test enters in context, every decision has a re-evaluation deadline.
renal.asideWho4: Chronic use of NSAIDs, PPIs, lithium
renal.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about kidney assessment.
renal.faq1Q: Why think about the kidney before any symptoms?
renal.faq1A: The kidney is the silent organ. It loses function on a curve — without pain, without symptoms — and only signals when the damage is already irreversible. About 10% of the Brazilian adult population has chronic kidney disease, and most don't know it. Detecting it early, in the window when damage is still reversible or stabilizable, changes the trajectory of the next decade.
renal.faq2Q: Which tests detect early kidney changes?
renal.faq2A: Serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) are the basics — but insufficient on their own. The combination that changes clinical decisions: cystatin C (more sensitive in early stages), albuminuria (urinary albumin/creatinine ratio), urinalysis with microscopy, electrolytes, 24-hour blood pressure when indicated. ApoB and the metabolic profile enter because the kidney and the cardiovascular system are coupled.
renal.faq3Q: Who should have a preventive kidney assessment?
renal.faq3A: Anyone over 40. Anyone with hypertension, diabetes, obesity, or metabolic syndrome at any age. Anyone with a family history of kidney disease, early cardiovascular event, or a single kidney. Athletes who use intense protein supplementation or chronic anti-inflammatories. Patients on prolonged use of PPIs, lithium, or non-steroidal anti-inflammatories.
renal.faq4A: In people with normal kidney function, the evidence is reassuring for creatine, omega-3, vitamin D, and magnesium. Concern concentrates on high doses of protein in those already with reduced function, anti-inflammatories used chronically without indication, unregulated imported supplements, and "kidney detox" formulas — which lack evidence and may mask real problems.
renal.faq5Q: What changes between an assessment by a nephrologist vs a general practitioner?
renal.faq5A: The nephrologist reads the same tests with a magnifying glass: pattern of eGFR decline, fine interpretation of albuminuria by stage, medication adjustment by residual function, decisions about nephroprotectors in pre-clinical phase. For an asymptomatic patient, it is the difference between a stamp and a plan.
renal.faq6A: Yes. Dr. Getúlio Amaral Filho is a nephrologist with RQE 16.038, faculty member at Santa Casa de Londrina and coordinator of the nephrology medical residency. Preventive kidney assessment is a structured part of the Continuum Plenya program, integrated with the cardiometabolic and functional reading.

mfi.metaTitle: Integrative functional medicine — clinical approach in Londrina
mfi.metaDescription: Conventional medicine practiced with more time, more listening, and systemic reading. Evidence-based intervention cascade. Plenya, Londrina, Brazil.
mfi.ogDescription: Not an alternative. Conventional medicine with time, listening, and judgment.
mfi.schemaDescription: Conventional medicine practiced with more time, listening, and systemic reading. Evidence-based intervention cascade.
mfi.heroTitle: Why this patient, by this route, now.
mfi.heroPEm2: why here, why now, why this way
mfi.heroPPart3: . It does not replace — it adds.
mfi.approachP1: Integrative functional medicine is neither alternative nor opposed to conventional medicine. It is conventional medicine practiced with a different visit length — 60 to 90 minutes — systemic listening, labs that go beyond the minimum, and a plan written in language that fits the patient's life.
mfi.approachP2: The logic is a cascade. First, habit — sleep, light exposure, food, movement, connection. Then supplementation guided by labs — no guesswork, no commercial bundles. Then medication, when the signal asks and habit is not enough. Procedures and surgery, when clearly indicated. The order matters because inverting it costs more and delivers less.
mfi.approachP3Part1: Dr. Getúlio Amaral Filho holds primary board certification in nephrology and internal medicine (RQE 16.038), and postgraduate training in integrative functional medicine through ABMFI. Functional does not replace the specialty — it adds. That is why Continuum Plenya has a multidisciplinary team: physician, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist, each with their own reading of the same patient.
mfi.approachP4: Everything we recommend passes through published evidence. There are no esoteric therapies, no unregistered tools, no out-of-scope work. What differentiates is time, depth, and judgment — not exotic instruments.
mfi.asideCascade3: Medication, when habit is not enough
mfi.asideHelps2: Chronic fatigue with no obvious cause
mfi.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about integrative functional medicine.
mfi.faq1A: It is a clinical approach that begins with the question "why this patient, by this route, now?" — not just "what is the name of this condition?" It treats systems (digestive, hormonal, mitochondrial, immune) as a coupled network, integrates habit, exposure, and laboratory data, and proposes intervention in a cascade: habit before supplement, supplement before medication, medication before procedure.
mfi.faq2Q: How does it differ from conventional medicine?
mfi.faq2A: It does not replace — it integrates. Conventional medicine is irreplaceable for diagnosing established disease and acute treatment. Integrative functional medicine works before (primary prevention), in between (functional causes that don't fit a traditional diagnosis), and after (metabolic follow-up for those already ill). The practical difference: visit length, depth of history, labs ordered, and the language of the plan.
mfi.faq3A: No. It is conventional medicine practiced with more time, more listening, more systemic reading, and more judgment in recommending habit, supplementation, and medication. Everything we recommend passes through published evidence. There are no esoteric therapies or anything outside the scope of the Brazilian Federal Council of Medicine (CFM).
mfi.faq4Q: Is the physician's training in functional medicine recognized?
mfi.faq4A: Dr. Getúlio's training in integrative functional medicine is through ABMFI (Brazilian Association of Integrative Functional Medicine) — an institution that follows international standards and requires prior medical training plus a CFM-recognized specialty. Functional does not replace the specialty; it adds to it. Dr. Getúlio holds primary board certification in nephrology (RQE 16.038) and internal medicine.
mfi.faq5Q: Which conditions respond best to the functional approach?
mfi.faq5A: Metabolic syndrome and pre-diabetes in a reversible phase, chronic fatigue with no obvious cause, sleep and circadian rhythm disorders, hormonal changes in men (testosterone) and women (peri- and post-menopause), functional digestive symptoms, subclinical nutritional deficiencies, chronic pain related to low-grade systemic inflammation. Always as a complement to managing the underlying disease, never as a substitute.
mfi.faq6Q: How long until I see results?
mfi.faq6A: Depends on the target. Sleep, energy, and digestive symptoms usually respond in 4 to 8 weeks. Metabolic markers (HbA1c, lipid profile) in 12 to 16 weeks. Body composition and VO₂ max in 16 to 24 weeks. Everything is measured at scheduled re-evaluation — without re-evaluation, there is no functional medicine, there is marketing.

healthspan.metaTitle: Healthspan — living well for longer, with evidence
healthspan.metaDescription: Healthspan is the time of life lived with functional autonomy. Plenya's program extends the fullness phase with VO₂ max, strength, metabolic markers, and longitudinal follow-up.
healthspan.ogDescription: The difference between how many years you live and how many you live well. The agenda of contemporary medicine.
healthspan.schemaDescription: The difference between lifespan and healthspan. Plenya's program extends the fullness phase with VO₂ max, strength, metabolic markers, and longitudinal follow-up.
healthspan.heroPPart1: Lifespan is how many years you live.
healthspan.heroPPart2: is how many of those years you live with autonomy, clarity, and energy. The medicine of the 20th century extended the first. Contemporary medicine answers for the second.
healthspan.windowP1: In Brazil, healthy life expectancy hovers around 65 years — total life expectancy, around 76. The gap is more than a decade lived with functional decline: pain, dependency, cognitive frailty, sarcopenia. Closing that gap is the agenda of healthspan.
healthspan.windowP2: It is not done with anti-aging promises, exotic supplements, or proprietary lab panels lacking validation. It is done with the few markers literature has shown to be predictive: cardiorespiratory capacity (VO₂ max), grip strength, appendicular muscle mass, ApoB, fasting and post-prandial glucose, hs-CRP, measured sleep.
healthspan.windowP3: The most valuable window to intervene is between 35 and 55 years old. That's when insulin sensitivity begins to fall, muscle mass declines ~1% per year without training, sleep fragments, and the first cardiovascular markers shift — but it is all still reversible at low cost. Waiting for symptoms means trading a cheap intervention for an expensive one.
healthspan.windowP4: Healthspan, at Plenya, is a measure — not a slogan. Every clinical decision passes through the Plenya Score: over 800 items organized into four pillars (Activity, Alimentation & Smart Adjuncts; Clinical Optimization; Tending Mind, Body & Bonds; Sleep, Rhythm & Recovery). Follow-up is longitudinal — we compare you with yourself, semester by semester.
healthspan.asideContinuumDesc: Six-month or annual, multidisciplinary team, single plan — Plenya Score as the measure.
healthspan.yes3: Individualized plan, revised every six months
healthspan.faq1Q: What's the difference between lifespan and healthspan?
healthspan.faq1A: Lifespan is how long you live. Healthspan is how much of that time you live with autonomy, clarity, and energy. Conventional medicine optimized lifespan in the 20th century; the 21st-century challenge is closing the distance between the two — today, on average, the last 8 to 12 years of Brazilian life are lived with significant functional loss.
healthspan.faq2Q: Is healthspan the same as anti-aging medicine?
healthspan.faq2A: No. Anti-aging medicine promises to reverse the clock, often without solid evidence. Healthspan is a measurable agenda: cardiorespiratory capacity (VO₂ max), strength and muscle mass, metabolic markers, cognition, sleep. The focus is extending the phase of functional fullness, not chasing immortality.
healthspan.faq3Q: Which markers really matter for healthspan?
healthspan.faq3A: The most robust in the literature: VO₂ max (the strongest predictor of all-cause mortality ever studied), grip strength, appendicular muscle mass, ApoB, glycated hemoglobin, hs-CRP, vitamin D, omega-3 index, measured sleep quality (not just duration). The Plenya Score integrates over 800 items in this direction.
healthspan.faq4Q: At what age does it make sense to think about healthspan?
healthspan.faq4A: The most valuable window is between 35 and 55 years old — before damage takes hold, after liver metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and muscle mass begin to decline silently. But the approach is useful at any age: at 30 for construction, at 60 for reversing what is still reversible.
healthspan.faq5Q: Is the Continuum Plenya program a healthspan approach?
healthspan.faq5A: Yes. The Continuum is Plenya's structured program for healthspan — six-month or annual, with a multidisciplinary team (physician, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist), specific labs, individualized exercise plan, and longitudinal follow-up measured by the Plenya Score.
healthspan.faq6A: It does not promise a cure, does not promise to reverse established diseases, does not promise immortality. It promises to give you evidence-based instruments to reach 70, 80, or 90 years old with more autonomy than expected for the average of your generation — which is, in itself, a transformation.

cases.c1Resumo: Lab panel within "normal" range, but several markers far from functional optimal. What looked like age was low storage compounded by fragmented sleep.
cases.c1Contexto: She came to Plenya after two annual checkups that returned "all normal." Main complaint: persistent fatigue, drop in libido, slow bowel, and the sense that "my mind doesn't respond the same way."
cases.c1A4: Fragmented sleep documented by wearable — 3 awakenings/night
cases.c1Co1: Iron repletion with the nutritionist, adjusted by absorption
cases.c1Co2: Vitamin D supplementation at a weight-calculated dose

cases.c1E2: Vitamin D 52 ng/mL over the same period
cases.c1E4: Quarterly re-evaluation of the Plenya Score, with review of the Activity and Sleep pillars
cases.c2Resumo: HbA1c at 6.3 detected in a routine checkup. No complaint, no weight to lose in the mirror. The combination of dietary change, strength training and treatment of sleep apnea brought the markers back into the normal range — without oral medication.
cases.c2Contexto: He brought a corporate exam with HbA1c 6.3% and fasting glucose 108 mg/dL. BMI 26.5. Trained 2x/week, "reasonable" diet. Type-2 diabetic father.
cases.c2A5: Sleep: 5h30 on average, with mild apnea on polysomnography

cases.c3A2: DHEA-S in the low range for her age

howItWorks.metaTitle: How It Works — Plenya medicine in four steps
howItWorks.metaDescription: Assess, interpret, personalized plan, and re-evaluate in cycle. How Plenya care enters your life — from the free Screening to the Continuum.
howItWorks.heroTitle: Four steps. Care that evolves with you.
howItWorks.heroP: Plenya medicine does not fit into one consultation — it fits into a cycle. Assess broadly, interpret deeply, act with a written plan, re-evaluate with method. And start again, at the point the data asked for.
howItWorks.faq1AAfter: of the Plenya Score — about 35 questions in a few minutes, no signup. The result already shows where your health stands today and what the next step is: a single Plenya Consultation or the Continuum.
howItWorks.faq2Q: Is the consultation in person or online?
howItWorks.faq2A: The Plenya Consultation can be in person (Londrina, Brazil) or online via telemedicine, with the same clinical depth. Continuum Plenya is 100% online — all weekly team meetings happen by video call.
howItWorks.faq3A: No. We see patients on a private-pay basis only. In Brazil, medical expenses are tax-deductible as health spending under current law.
howItWorks.faq4Q: How long until I see results?
howItWorks.faq4A: The first clinical reading happens at the initial consultation itself. In the Continuum, the Score curve typically shows movement between the first and third months — that's when the first plan adjustments mature.
howItWorks.faq5A: In the Continuum, after the plan is built, a personalized box arrives at your door — curated items from the team and supplements or compounded medications specific to your protocol. New boxes follow the rhythm of the plan.
howItWorks.faq6Q: Can I cancel the Continuum if I change my mind?
howItWorks.faq6A: Yes. Enrollment and cancellation terms are presented in direct conversation before signing, based on the modality you choose (six-month or annual).
howItWorks.exitTitle: Start with the Screening. In five minutes you have the first reading.
howItWorks.step1Body: You complete the Plenya Score — the free Screening or the full version in consultation — and the team organizes your history, symptoms, labs, habits, and medications into a single panel.
howItWorks.step2Body: The physician — and, in the Continuum, the entire team — performs a functional reading of your expanded lab panel. It's not "it's normal": it's what is far from optimal, what deserves intervention, and what can wait.
howItWorks.step3Body: A written plan agreed with you, organized by the four pillars of The ACTS Method — medication when indicated, lifestyle adjustments, supplementation and referrals when the case calls for it. In the Continuum, a single plan built by the four professionals — physician, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist.
howItWorks.step4Body: Every three months (Continuum), or as clinically indicated, a new Score. The curve shows real progress, stagnation, or decline. The data guide the next clinical decision — without depending on memory or the impression of whoever is looking.
howItWorks.step4Detail: Visible evolving curve for you and the team

score.metaTitle: Plenya Score — measurement instrument of The ACTS Method
score.metaDescription: Over 800 items — history, symptoms, labs, habits, and medications — translated into a clear, evolving, personalized score. The single measure of your health.
score.heroP: The measurement instrument of The ACTS Method. Over 800 items — history, symptoms, labs, habits, and medications — translated into a clear, evolving, personalized score of your health.
score.whatTitle: The Plenya Score does not replace a lab test. It fills the void between them.
score.whatP: It is the measure care needed in order to stop being a disconnected sequence of visits and become a process with direction and visible progress. Where before there were isolated reports, now there is a score that synthesizes — and that evolves with each re-evaluation.
score.howTitle: Three steps. A score that makes sense.
score.step1Body: Over 800 items are gathered — clinical and family history, current symptoms, lab tests, lifestyle habits, current medications, genetic markers. There are no idle questions: every item feeds a clinical decision.
score.step2Body: Each item enters a clinical pillar of The ACTS Method — grouped under one of the four letters: Activity, Alimentation & Smart Adjuncts; Clinical Optimization; Tending Mind, Body & Bonds; Sleep, Rhythm & Recovery.
score.step3Body: You receive an overall score and one per letter. With each re-evaluation, the curve shows what improved, what plateaued, and where the next intervention needs to enter.
score.scoreP1Pt1: You receive an overall score and four scores per ACTS letter. Together, they form a constellation — where strength is concentrated, where the gap lives.
score.scoreP2: When the radar is symmetric, care is distributed. When one tip sinks, that is where the next intervention enters.
score.bandsCaptionPart1: The band is not a verdict — it is the starting point of the next clinical conversation. A
score.bandsCaptionPart2: from 85% tells a different story than a
score.evolutionTitle: The curve that shows whether care is working.
score.evolutionP: With each re-evaluation, a new point enters the curve. The physician, the team, and you see the same chart: real progress, plateau, or decline — an objective reading that guides the next clinical decision.
score.evolutionChartAria: Example of a Plenya Score evolution curve
score.tiersDesc: From the free public screening to continuous care applied by the team. Each level is an entry point — choose by the moment you're in.
score.tier1Desc: Public, free version. About 35 questions answered in a few minutes — no signup. A first reading of where your health stands and what the next step is.
score.tier2Desc: A clinical deep-dive with the physician, in person or online. Focused on the priority goals identified in the plan, based on the expanded biomarker panel.
score.tier3Desc: Full version, applied by the Plenya team across the program. Comprehensive clinical, laboratory, behavioral, and functional assessment — with a single plan, personalized goals, and re-evaluation each cycle.
score.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about the Plenya Score.
score.faq1Q: Does the Plenya Score replace my labs?
score.faq1A: No. The Score organizes and gives direction to your labs, symptoms, and habits — it does not replace them. It is the integrated reading that was missing between one visit and the next.
score.faq2A: Yes. The Screening is the public, free version of the Score — about 35 questions in a few minutes, no signup. The result already shows where your health stands and what the next step is.
score.faq3Q: How long does the Screening take?
score.faq3A: About 5 minutes. Just questions — no need to have your labs at hand.
score.faq4Q: How does the Score evolve over time?
score.faq4A: In Continuum Plenya, the Score is repeated every three months. The curve shows what advanced, what plateaued, and where the next intervention needs to enter.
score.faq5Q: What are the bands and what do they mean?
score.faq5A: Critical (0-30), Caution (31-50), Regular (51-70), Good (71-85), Optimal (86-100). The band is not a verdict — it is the starting point of the next clinical conversation.
score.faq6A: Yes. The public Screening is anonymous by default. In the Continuum, data is stored in line with our Privacy Policy and Brazil's LGPD law (similar in scope to GDPR).
score.exitTitleLine1: The Score shows where you are.
score.exitTitleLine2: The ACTS Method is how we act from there.

continuum.metaDescription: Continuum Plenya is Plenya's six-month or annual program. 100% online care with a multidisciplinary team — physician, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — organized by The ACTS Method and measured by the Plenya Score.
continuum.heroPPart1: Health is not solved in one consultation. It is built over time — together, with method. Six or twelve months led by the
continuum.problemTitle: The conventional check-up does not look for what will take you out of the game. By the time it finds it, you are already sick.
continuum.problemP1: Between the lab that reads "normal" and the diagnosis that changes your life lies a silent window of ten to twenty years. Inside it, small symptoms accumulate, biomarkers begin to drift within the "acceptable range" — and no one investigates, because no one is looking.
continuum.problemP2: Reacting only after problems show themselves is the most expensive bet you can place on your own health. The Continuum exists for those who decided to step out of that pattern.
continuum.aboutTitle: Some look for health once something has shown up. Continuum Plenya exists for those who chose the opposite path.
continuum.aboutP1: A Plenya Consultation begins your relationship with your managing physician. The Continuum deepens that relationship over time — months or years with the clinician who oversees your care longitudinally and aligns your plan between Plenya's team and the doctors already caring for you outside the clinic (cardiologist, endocrinologist, gynecologist). Twenty years of clinical practice taught a simple truth: living longer is not living well. Health is built over time — together, with method, and with presence — or it is not built at all.
continuum.aboutP2: It begins with the complete Plenya Score — a full clinical, laboratory, behavioral and functional assessment applied by the team — and continues in steady rhythm: a weekly meeting with one of the four professionals, a cycle that completes every four weeks, quarterly re-evaluations, and a structured close at the end of the period. No pillar of The ACTS Method goes unreviewed.
continuum.forWhomTitle: Continuum Plenya is not for everyone.
continuum.forWhomDesc: It is for those who recognize one of these moments. Not as a diagnosis — but as the point in life when it makes sense to build health over time, together, with method.
continuum.fw1Title: Doing everything right — and the signals don't add up.
continuum.fw1Body: Trains, eats well, sleeps. Even so, energy doesn't return, the gut acts up, the skin loses its glow, three viruses a year. Small symptoms that, together, describe a terrain wearing down.
continuum.fw2Body: A lab result that startled you, a family diagnosis, a birthday that hurt. The window seemed far away and suddenly came too close.
continuum.fw3Body: Partners, team, children, parents — people depend on you whole. Health became a critical variable in what you sustain.
continuum.fw4Title: In a transition no one names.
continuum.fw4Body: Sleep, mood, body — something is changing and the clinical answer is "it's nothing yet" or "it's just age." There's no map.
continuum.fw5Title: Too much information, not enough integration.
continuum.fw5Body: Trainer, dietitian, therapist, physician — each in their own corner. Wearables, dashboards, reports — data in surplus, decisions missing.
continuum.fw6Title: Wanting to be whole for those still to arrive.
continuum.fw6Body: A small child at 45, projects that don't fit in ten years. The question is no longer how long will I live — it became how will I be when they need me.
continuum.honestyDesc: The earlier we align expectations, the better the care works — and the more we respect the time of those still to arrive.
continuum.notForB1: An acute symptom, a specific question, one set of labs to interpret — that's solved in a Plenya Consultation. The Continuum is a six- or twelve-month commitment.
continuum.notForB2: The Continuum will not change what you don't want to change. But it also will not work without willingness. The team proposes, returns the data, adjusts together — you execute.
continuum.notForB3: We are not an urgent-care service. The WhatsApp group answers questions during business hours — it does not replace an emergency room or on-call clinic.
continuum.doubtTitle: Not sure if any of those portraits is yours?
continuum.doubtDesc: Five short questions return which portraits of the program most match your moment. No diagnosis, no data capture.
continuum.teamDesc: Physician, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist meet before your first encounter, discuss your case, and design an integrated plan. Every clinical decision speaks to the others.
continuum.howTitle: One front per week. All present every month.
continuum.howDesc: In the four-week cycle, each pillar of The ACTS Method is addressed by a responsible professional — under the longitudinal clinical management of your managing physician, who maintains continuity of the plan and coordinates with the doctors caring for you outside Plenya. No pillar goes without monthly review.
continuum.covRQuem: Crosses all four, under clinical coordination
continuum.timelineTitle: From day zero to the next horizon.
continuum.j1Body: An online consultation with each of the four professionals at different points in the week — starting with the physician. Together, they fill out the Plenya Score, which sets the starting point — and the direction. When indicated, additional labs are ordered.
continuum.j2Body: The four professionals meet, discuss the case, and build an integrated initial plan aligned with your goals. Then, in an online opening session, the physician returns the clinical reading and presents the full plan. No one prescribes alone.
continuum.j3Body: Each week, an online meeting with one of the four professionals. Every four weeks the cycle completes — every area of ACTS is reviewed and reinforced month after month.
continuum.j4Body: After the plan is built, a personalized box arrives at your door — curated items from the team and supplements or compounded medications specific to your protocol. As care evolves and the plan adjusts, new boxes follow the same rhythm — prepared whenever clinically indicated.
continuum.j5Body: Follow-up labs as clinically indicated and a new round of the Plenya Score. The curve shows what advanced, what plateaued, and where the next intervention enters.
continuum.j6Body: At the end of six or twelve months, a structured assessment closes the period. From there, we decide together how to design the next cycle.
continuum.modSemestralBody: Full cycle: initial assessment, integrated plan, weekly meetings, quarterly re-evaluation, and close.
continuum.modAnualBody: Same structure, with one additional quarterly re-evaluation and deeper consolidation of habits over time.
continuum.modPriceText: On request. The team presents the conditions in direct conversation, based on the modality you choose.

continuum.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about the Continuum.
continuum.faq1Q: Why is the Continuum different from only Plenya Consultations?
continuum.faq1A: Every Plenya Consultation already begins the relationship with the managing physician. The Continuum deepens that relationship over time — multidisciplinary team discussing your case, a single written plan, weekly meetings, and quarterly re-evaluations. The Plenya Score shows the evolution as a curve.
continuum.faq2Q: Can it be combined with my reference physician?
continuum.faq2A: Yes. The Continuum is complementary. Clinical coordination stays with the Plenya physician, but ongoing treatments with other professionals continue — with integrated reading, and nothing is changed without alignment.
continuum.faq3Q: How long until I see results?
continuum.faq3A: The first clinical reading happens at the initial consultation itself. The Score curve typically shows movement between the first and third months — that's when the first adjustments mature.
continuum.faq4Q: Is the Continuum online or in person?
continuum.faq4A: 100% online. All weekly team meetings happen via video call. The Plenya Box ships to you by mail.
continuum.faq5A: Curated items chosen by the team and supplements or compounded medications specific to your protocol, based on clinical indication. As care evolves, new boxes are prepared.
continuum.faq6A: Through direct conversation with the team, after an initial alignment call. Conditions and payment options are presented based on the modality you choose (six-month or annual).
continuum.faq7Q: Can I cancel if I change my mind?
continuum.faq7A: Yes. Cancellation conditions are presented before enrollment and follow Brazilian consumer protection law.

consultas.metaDescription: Private medical consultations at Plenya — in person in Londrina or online via telemedicine, with Dr. Getúlio Amaral and the clinic's other physicians.
consultas.heroP: Health is not about reacting. It is about anticipating. The medical consultation at Plenya is where that medicine begins — long-form listening, careful reading of the data, and clear next steps even when labs come back "normal."
consultas.aboutP1: We make time to listen. A medical consultation at Plenya does not fit into fifteen minutes — and was not designed to. We review your history, your prior labs, your sleep, your routine, your body composition, and what has changed since someone last truly looked.
consultas.aboutP2: We work with a functional reading of an expanded lab panel — biomarkers beyond the routine, read between the lab reference range and the optimal clinical range. The resulting plan is organized by The ACTS Method (Activity & Alimentation · Clinical Optimization · Tending Mind & Body · Sleep & Rhythm) and may include medication, lifestyle adjustment, supplementation, or referral to the multidisciplinary team — as the case calls for.
consultas.aboutP3Part1: Every Plenya Consultation begins or continues your relationship with your managing physician — the Plenya clinician who oversees your care longitudinally, aligning your plan with the team here and with the doctors you already see outside the clinic (cardiologist, endocrinologist, gynecologist). They work with a clinical focus of the Plenya Score — a deep dive on the priority goals identified in your plan, based on the expanded lab panel. Clinical continuity does not depend on the Continuum program: it begins at your first consultation and stays through every visit thereafter. When care calls for Plenya's integrated team — nutrition, psychology, exercise, in structured cycles — the next step is called

drGetulio.metaTitle: Dr. Getúlio Amaral Filho — Clinical Director
drGetulio.metaDescription: Brazilian physician, nephrologist, and specialist in integrative functional medicine. Clinical director of Plenya.
drGetulio.heroP1: Brazilian physician trained at the State University of Londrina (UEL) in 2004. Board-certified in nephrology and internal medicine through Santa Casa de Londrina, with formal certification from the Brazilian Society of Nephrology. He coordinates the nephrology residency at Santa Casa and serves as medical director of DaVita Intra Hospitalar de Londrina.
drGetulio.heroP2: His postgraduate training in integrative functional medicine through ABMFI underpins Plenya's positioning: medicine based on labs, data, and structured decision-making, applied years before the diagnosis takes hold.
drGetulio.aboutP1: Over two decades in internal medicine and nephrology, with much of that work conducted within the hospital setting. Daily practice meant following patients in advanced stages of kidney and cardiovascular disease — cases in which, often, the trajectory could have been changed years earlier, through routine decisions and more careful monitoring.
drGetulio.aboutP2: Integrative functional medicine is not an alternative to conventional medicine. It is a way of organizing preventive care in a structured way — labs, data, clinical decision-making — directed at what precedes disease.
drGetulio.aboutP3: At Plenya, Dr. Getúlio takes on the role of your managing physician — the clinician who knows your history in depth and oversees your care longitudinally, over months and years. He aligns your plan between Plenya's team and the doctors already caring for you outside the clinic — cardiologist, endocrinologist, gynecologist. Plenya does not replace these relationships: it ensures the clinical continuity of the whole, with someone who is finally looking at you as a whole person.

about.manifesto3: Living well is the reflection of what you choose every day.
about.manifesto4: It is awareness. It is freedom.
about.originP1Part1: Plenya was born from the passion of
about.originP1Part2: and the team that came together around him — physicians, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — for life in its full form and for longevity lived with clarity, energy, and purpose.
about.originP2: Across more than two decades between hospital wards, dialysis units, and the consulting office, Dr. Getúlio watched medicine save lives in critical conditions — and saw, in parallel, people living longer and living worse, fragmented across five or six clinicians who never spoke to one another. Patients with "normal" labs who were already falling ill in silence.
about.originP3Part1: Plenya is the clinical answer to that observation. A model designed to see earlier, follow closely, and act with clarity — focused on
about.originP4: Because living longer is no longer enough. What matters is how you live.
about.clinicCaption: Architectural render of the future Plenya headquarters. Reception and environment designed for hospitality and continuous care.
about.teamCaption: Physicians, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — a single team that meets, discusses the case, and designs an integrated plan of care.
about.purposeTitle: To guide people toward living longer and better, with autonomy over their own health.
about.purposeP1: In a landscape shaped by information overload and fragmented approaches, Plenya offers care that is integrated, personalized, and sustainable over time. We connect different areas of health into a single structured plan — built on data, proximity, and shared responsibility.
about.goldenTitle: Why we exist. How we care. What we deliver.
about.goldenWhy: Because people are living longer, but not necessarily better — and they continue to be treated in parts, not as a whole. No one should arrive at the most important phase of life limited by the choices made before.
about.goldenHow: Through integrated, continuous, and personalized care that connects different areas of health into a single structured plan — with data, proximity, and shared responsibility.
about.goldenWhat: A health and longevity program that combines a multidisciplinary team, a proprietary method (ACTS), and close follow-up to transform habits, body, and mind in a sustainable way.
about.agirSectionTitle: Four interdependent pillars for health that sustains over time.
about.agirSectionDesc: The clinical framework that organizes Plenya's care. It is not a protocol — it is a way of structuring medical follow-up around what sustains health over the long term.
about.agirSectionCta: Discover The ACTS Method in full
about.positioningTitle: Fragmented care is the problem. Integration is the answer.
about.positioningDesc: Today, the patient moves between different clinicians, sources of information, and conflicting advice — with no clarity, no continuity, and no single direction. At Plenya, we integrate clinical work, data, and close follow-up to turn care into a continuous, personalized, and measurable process.

method.metaDescription: The ACTS Method organizes Plenya's clinical care into four interdependent pillars — Activity, Alimentation & Smart Adjuncts; Clinical Optimization; Tending Mind, Body & Bonds; Sleep, Rhythm & Recovery. Medicine that anticipates, with depth.
method.heroTitle: ACTS — four pillars for health that sustains over time.
method.heroSubtitle: Plenya's clinical framework organizes care into four interdependent dimensions of health. It is not a protocol. It is the way we decide, monitor, and follow up — with the depth that longevity demands.
method.premiseTitle: The body does not wait for the diagnosis to fall ill.
method.premiseP1: By the time blood sugar climbs, insulin resistance has been building for a decade. By the time a heart attack happens, the plaque has been growing for twenty years. The window for intervention exists — but it closes in silence.
method.premiseP2: The ACTS Method is how we operate inside that window. Four interdependent pillars that, together, organize preventive care in a structured way — labs, data, clinical decision-making — directed at what comes before disease.
method.monitoredFootnote: Partial list — actual monitoring covers dozens of additional markers per pillar, tailored to your case.
method.convictionsTitle: Five sentences that took a decade to become convictions.
method.applyTitle: Applied by a team. Measured by the Plenya Score.
method.applyP1: The ACTS Method is the framework that organizes our clinical decisions and our communication with you. The Plenya Score translates your current state into a number that evolves throughout follow-up — so progress is clear, measurable, and shared.
method.applyP2: The rule of two operates here: we begin with two focuses, with clinical judgment, and advance at the pace of your body — not at the pace of well-meaning lists.
method.p1Territory: The three engines no medication can replace
method.p1Intro: Food is not fuel — it is information. Every meal instructs genes, modulates hormones, and feeds the microbiome. Exercise is one of the most powerful medications that exists. Supplementation corrects what the lab shows is missing. The three engines work together.
method.p1Quote: Medication takes care of what it reaches. The rest — insulin, inflammation, sarcopenia, microbiome — depends on what you do every day.
method.p1M4: Vitamin D, B12, iron, and omega-3 status
method.p2Intro: Hormones, biomarkers, data-guided pharmacology. The part of the work where the physician stops being a lifestyle counselor and becomes the pilot of a data dashboard — test, intervene, retest, adjust.
method.p2Quote: Ordering TSH alone is like checking the faucet pressure without verifying that water is coming out. Metabolic management begins by ordering the right test.
method.p2M1: Full hormone panel (free testosterone, SHBG, estradiol, DHEA-S, cortisol, thyroid)
method.p2M2: ApoB, lipoprotein(a), CAC score when indicated
method.p2M5: Genetic markers when indicated — precision medicine
method.p3Intro: The axis between psychology, the immune system, and inflammation. Psychological states directly alter immune, hormonal, and inflammatory function — not as metaphor, as mechanism. When the HPA axis is on chronic alert, no other pillar functions fully.
method.p3Quote: Ana optimized everything biochemistry would allow. The hs-CRP would not come down. What needed treatment was the anxiety she called personality.
method.p3M5: Quality of relationships and social support
method.p4Territory: The substrate on which the other pillars operate
method.p4Intro: Sleep, chronobiology, the synchronization of biological clocks. The suprachiasmatic nucleus is the conductor; every cell has its clock. When signals arrive at unpredictable times, the orchestra goes out of tune — and the name for that is chronodisruption.
method.p4Quote: When the substrate is compromised, everything built above starts to crack. Sleep is not a pillar like the others — it is the base.
method.p4M2: Symptoms and screening for obstructive sleep apnea
method.c1Text: The body does not wait for the diagnosis to fall ill.
method.c1Sub: Disease begins ten, fifteen, twenty years before the label. The window for intervention exists — but it closes. And it closes in silence.
method.c2Text: No one changes everything at once.
method.c2Sub: Two focuses per quarter, with measure and deadline. Those who try to change ten things on Monday usually have changed none by Friday.
method.c3Text: The pillars do not work in isolation.
method.c3Sub: Nutrition without sleep is wear-down. Exercise without recovery is overtraining. Hormones without mental health is optimization on sand.
method.c4Sub: No patient does it alone. Preventive medicine is networked work — physician, multidisciplinary team, and the patient at the center.
method.c5Text: The best time to start was ten years ago. The second-best time is today.
method.c5Sub: This is not a motivational line. It is clinical data. Reversibility decreases over time. The cost of inaction increases with age.
